proposal.name: Restore sandbox memory and time margin

issue_plan.name: Restore sandbox memory and time margin
issue_plan.summary: First move the three large recording heap stress tests into the existing CI integration lane, preserving their coverage and keeping small functional checks in ordinary tests. Then correct the real-checkout budget check to distinguish sampled anonymous and shared memory from reclaimable file cache, and report test durations and memory by phase. These two complete plumbing changes separate the expensive verify and plumbing package baselines: the combined plan's first check exceeded the check tool's fifteen-minute call limit without returning validation evidence. The four-CPU quota, container limits, worker count and production deadlines stay in place, and the merger verifies the finished change on a quiet machine.

issues.title: Run recording heap stress tests in the CI integration lane
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Recover time in ordinary plumbing sandboxes that touch internal/verify by moving only the large-recording workloads of TestGateRecordingPeakHeap, TestGateRefusedRecordingPeakHeap and TestPythonApplicationConversionPeakHeap behind the existing integration build tag. This is the first part of #599. CI measurements in its discussion put these tests at approximately 370, 133 and 68 seconds respectively; recent real-checkout runs put the verify touched-test phase against its twenty-minute limit under the four-CPU quota.

The tests currently live in internal/verify/gate_recording_stream_accept_test.go and internal/verify/python_application_recording_stream_accept_test.go. Read their shared fixtures, subprocess helpers and all related regression tests before planning the move. Preserve their registered stress-test names, all 32,768- and 65,536-entry workloads, Go and TypeScript routes, successful and deliberately bad or refused cases, sampled and explored Python conversion, exact heap ceilings, descriptor and cleanup assertions, recording-tail and coverage checks, subprocess timeouts and measurement settings. Their child processes must still select and execute the actual measured tests. Move the test entry points into an integration-tagged test file in the same package; shared helpers may remain available to ordinary tests.

The conversion test also contains inexpensive errors and validation cases and interleaved sampled lifecycle checks. Keep every one of those assertions in the default suite, under TestPythonApplicationConversionValidation, rather than moving them behind the tag with the large recordings. Preserve ordinary gate ownership, compatibility, cancellation, cleanup and refusal coverage. This changes where the stress workloads run, not the streaming implementation or what they require.

CI already invokes .github/shard-tests.sh with -tag integration for internal/verify. It selects the difference between tagged and ordinary test inventories, so the three stress names must be absent from the ordinary inventory and present in the tagged inventory; default-registered tests that merely skip would not satisfy this coverage requirement. Use the existing lane without changing anything under .github/ or adding a new environment opt-in. Add acceptance coverage that checks the real inventories, confirms ordinary functional cases still run, and prevents loss or duplication of the stress entry points. Run the full stress family with go test -tags=integration ./internal/verify -run '^(TestGateRecordingPeakHeap|TestGateRefusedRecordingPeakHeap|TestPythonApplicationConversionPeakHeap)$' -count=1 -timeout 20m, as well as the appropriate ordinary checks; preserve existing integration CI coverage and timeouts.

Keep the default four-CPU quota, eight sandbox workers, 4 GiB and 1,024-process limits, check queue and existing ordinary and verify deadlines. Update SPEC.md with existing decision citations and docs/factory.md with the default-versus-integration coverage and the explicit stress command. The README already links that detail page and need not grow. The merger records the new test scheduling decision refining D-0333, the streaming recording and heap-ceiling decision, while preserving D-0281, D-0313 and D-0350. The change is tested plumbing under D-0105, with documentation maintained under D-0122 and D-0294; a factory build cannot write decisions/.

issues.title: Measure sandbox working memory and report where checks spend time
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Finish #599 after the recording heap stress tests have moved into the CI integration lane. Correct TestSandboxBudgetAndRealCheckout so reclaimable file cache filling a cgroup does not count as exhausting working memory, and provide the measurements needed to assess the remaining time and memory margin. The issue's control reached memory.peak equal to a 512 MiB limit with only 128 KiB of anon memory, roughly 510 MiB of file pages, and zero OOM events or kills. Its real sandboxes have likewise reached exactly 4 GiB without OOM events.

Read internal/plumbing/sandbox_budget_accept_test.go, its embedded Docker observer, internal/plumbing/sandbox_cpu_observer_regression_test.go, sandbox.go, sandbox_runner.py, and the existing shard, phase, timing, interruption, cleanup and summary tests and command fakes before naming files. Extend the real-budget observer to sample memory.stat anon and shmem throughout the container's lifetime, including compilation and test execution, using a bounded low-overhead sampler. Judge memory by the maximum of anon plus shmem from each individual sample, never by adding maxima observed at different times. Fail if that sampled sum reaches or exceeds memory.max, if memory.events records any oom or oom_kill, or if required counters or sampling evidence are missing, malformed or unavailable. Preserve the existing process-peak and denied-process failures and the checks of enforced limits and CPU quota. Keep reporting the kernel memory.peak and memory.events max counter as diagnostic data, including when file cache fills the cap. State the sampling interval and the fact that a sampled peak is not a kernel-maintained high-water mark.

Retain host-side resource reports on normal exit, failure, cancellation and forced removal. Sample during work, preserve earlier peaks after usage falls, take a bounded final observation when possible, and merge observations without losing cumulative OOM, process or CPU evidence. A late removal race must not erase a valid completed report, while an incomplete observation must not hide a sampling failure or substitute for final required evidence. Observer failures must fail the opt-in check and must not prevent delegation of cleanup. Preserve exactly one identified report per container. Keep the complete existing cpu.max, cpu.stat and elapsed-time reporting.

Make the sandbox's measured per-test elapsed_seconds survive parsing into Result.TestResults, retaining package, test, phase, status and worker identities and distinguishing an absent measurement from measured zero. These are measured results, not the untrusted scheduling-cache hints. Add explicit phase-start records that allow the observer to distinguish preparation, compilation, touched-test execution and acceptance, and report sampled anon-plus-shmem peaks and sample counts by phase. Have the real budget check log a bounded list of the slowest completed top-level tests with their package, phase and elapsed time, alongside phase memory, CPU and wall-time evidence. Preserve compact ordinary summaries, failure and unfinished identities, scheduling, verdicts, acceptance attribution and timing-cache behavior.

Add daemon-free acceptance and regression coverage using the actual observer and runner with local cgroup files and command-boundary fixtures. Cover file-cache saturation without OOM, sampled working memory reaching the cap, OOM without a kill, OOM kills, process exhaustion, missing counters and samples, peaks occurring before exit, the maximum of contemporaneous anon-plus-shmem sums, phase attribution, and persistence through cancellation and removal. Exercise real fixture test execution to check retained durations and phase boundaries without relying on the expensive stress tests. Update existing resource-observer fixtures that pin the old report shape and accounting rule; retain their CPU and cleanup assertions.

Keep the four-CPU default and its existing host override, eight workers, 4 GiB and 1,024-process caps, queue behavior, ten/twelve-minute ordinary budgets and twenty/twenty-five-minute verify budgets. The real check still runs two simultaneous fresh-cache sandboxes that must both pass before twenty-five minutes, then three fresh-cache sandboxes that must all return within twenty-six minutes fifteen seconds, with named partial results allowed in that second wave. Image acquisition stays outside the timed runs. The integration stress coverage established by the preceding change remains in CI.

Update SPEC.md with existing decision citations and docs/factory.md with the corrected memory rule, report fields and sampling limitations, diagnostic procedure and merger evidence. Keep the README's existing link to that detail page. The merger records the new accounting and measurement decision refining D-0281 and D-0313 and preserving D-0350; D-0105, D-0122 and D-0294 govern plumbing and documentation, and the build cannot write decisions/.

Under Merger work, rerun INVARIANT_PLUMBING_REAL=1 go test ./internal/plumbing -run '^TestSandboxBudgetAndRealCheckout$' -count=1 -timeout 70m on a quiet cgroup-v2 Docker host with no factory checks competing, using the default four-CPU quota. Record checkout identities, image and host configuration, each sandbox's elapsed time, slowest tests, memory by phase, sampled working-memory peak, kernel peak, max events, OOM and process counters, CPU usage and throttling, and each wave's result. Compare with pre-change measurements on the same host where available, identify measurement differences or missing baseline evidence explicitly, and do not claim an unmeasured speedup or capacity pass. Docker-dependent capacity measurement and decision recording remain merger work; applicable real Python and TLAPS suites remain required CI checks.
